 Judgment

These appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act have been filed against the judgment and award dated April 2, 2018, passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Arsikere (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No. 66/2016.
2. The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs. 15,00,000.

It is the claimants' NC: 2024:KHC:21274 case that on May 18, 2014, due to the rash and negligent driving of the autorickshaw bearing registration No. KA-13-A-5319, an accident Sri. Lokesh. K vs Smt. Rekha on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178439652/
3 occurred.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs. 10,93,000 along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

However, the respondent denied the manner of the accident as narrated by the petitioners and claimed their discharge from liability on the ground that the driver of the autorickshaw was not holding a valid driving license on the date of the accident.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company and perused the records.
4.
Exhibit R1 is the extract of the Driving License of the alleged driver of the autorickshaw vehicle.
The driver held a three- wheeler non-transport license but did not possess a three-wheeler transport driving license.

The Supreme Court, in the case of *Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd.*, reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663, ruled as follows:
"A person having a license to drive a light motor vehicle would be entitled to drive any motor vehicle of gross vehicle weight less than 7500 kg."

sentences.text: Therefore, although the driver was holding a three-wheeler non- transport license, he would be capable of driving a three-wheeler transport vehicle.
5. The accident occurred in 2014, and at the time of the accident, the deceased was 34 years old.

In the absence of proof of income, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs. 8,500 per month, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, in contrast to the Rs.7,000 assessed by the Tribunal.
The NC: 2024:KHC:21274 Tribunal did not award 'future prospects' and deducted one-fourth of the annual income towards personal and living expenses.

An additional 40%
of the assessed income has to be added to the income of the deceased towards future prospects.
Given the deceased's age of 34 years, a multiplier of 16 is applied.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to Rs. 17,13,600 (calculated as Rs. 8,500 + Rs. 3,400 - Rs. 2,975 x 12 x 16) towards loss of dependency and *Rs.1,20,000/-(40,000X3) is awarded toward loss of love and affections.

7. Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is a reassessed as follows :

 1. Loss of dependency 10,08,000/- 17,13,600/-
 2. Loss of consortium to  40,000/- 40,000-/-
 Petitioner No.1  *3. Loss of love and  Nil 1,20,000-/-
 affections  4. Loss transport and  30,000/- 15,000-/-
 funeral expenses  5. Loss of estate 15,000/- 15,000-/-
 Total 10,93,000/- *19,03,600/-

Accordingly, I pass the following :
ORDER i. Appeals are disposed of.
ii.
The claimants are entitled for total compensation amount of *Rs.19,03,600/- with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till actual realisation.
The entire compensation shall be deposited by the respondent No.2-Insurance Company in favour of the claimants within a period of twelve weeks.
iv. The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the appellant in *M.F.A.No.1477/2019 subject to furnishing identity proof.
*v. The amount in deposit in M.F.A.No.6106/2018 is ordered to be refunded to the appellant.
Consequently pending I.A's does not survive for consideration and accordingly disposed of.
